body: Why do cells need to share views?

Maybe i don't undeerstand Cell concept. But...
Example:
FirstCell generates list of Users
SecondCell generate list of Roles
and set for cell view two vars: $fieldName, $options
Both templates contains same code like:

```
echo $this->Form->input($fieldName, $options);
```

At now I need to create two templates for two cell. Why shoudn't reuse existing one?

P.S. This is just an idea. You better know whether to implement it.

Ok.. Example of my code...

```
$cell = $this->cell('FirstCell', ['key' => "Article.0.text", 'options' => ['type' => 'text']]);
echo $cell->render('../SecondCell/display');
```

Output: 

```
Missing View
Error: The view for ArticlesController::index() was not found.
Confirm you have created the file: second_cell/display.ctp  in one of the following paths:
/home/myuser/projects/app3/src/Template/second_cell/display.ctp
...
```

It seems that cells somehow in this case take affect as the parent view render process. I have used last commit from branch 3.0
Ok, I can make the call style I suggested work. I think that is a simple solution that behaves the same as controller view files and elements.

@markstory I think you set wrong milestone for this issue. As I understand it should be 3.0.0
Thank's for your job and great framework.

issue.body:
Relative paths in view file names where handled very poorly before when subdirectories were involved. This was not very important in 2.x but is more important for 3.x as we have Cells and relative paths should work
properly.

Refs #3945

body: After talking a look I've opened #3986 to fix this issue. Currently `View` does very silly things when relative paths are involved. I'm going to close this issue as the method I suggested will work once #3986 has been merged.
Just so I'm clear, you have a cell in a plugin, and you are trying to render an alternate view?
Awesome, I'll try to get a fix together tonight. Thanks for using cells in ways I hadn't considered :+1:
